title: The Slow Garden
premise: Jonah Fairweather, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter who writes romance novels but refuses to live one, inherits half of a failing coastal orchard alongside Elias Thorne — the boy who left her twelve years ago and never explained why. Forced to share one growing season to save the land from a developer's deadline, they must prune old trees and older grievances, uncovering that Elias left to protect her from her father's debts and his own family's ruin. As harvest nears, Jonah learns the heart cannot be trained or contained, only risked whole; she chooses him publicly at the orchard auction, and together they keep the garden — and each other.
about_author: Beatrix Iversen is a former marine archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction. She lives on a windswept peninsula with an ill-tempered cat and an overgrown apple tree she refuses to cut down.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A solicitor's letter reveals Jonah has inherited half of Fairweather Orchard — co-owned with Elias Thorne, the man who vanished from her life without goodbye. She rereads his last unsent letter, hardens her heart, and drives out to see the land. Emotional beat: guarded grief disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Fight
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He arrives expecting to sell his half; Jonah arrives to stop him. Their first confrontation in the frost-killed orchard is all old wounds and new accusations. A developer's offer letter falls from his coat, and Jonah realizes they have thirty days before the bank forecloses. Emotional beat: anger as armor.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They strike a reluctant bargain: one season, shared labor, no questions about the past. Jonah moves into the drafty farmhouse; Elias sleeps in the packing shed. Small domestic collisions — shared kettles, disputed ladders — begin eroding her defenses. Emotional beat: wary truce with sparks underneath.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Pruning the oldest apple tree, they find initials carved by their grandparents — who once loved across the same family feud. Elias almost explains why he left, then retreats when Jonah's father's name surfaces in old debt ledgers. Emotional beat: tenderness interrupted by buried history.

chapters.title: The Developer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The developer's representative turns out to be Marisol, Elias's estranged sister, offering him a clean exit if he signs. Torn between escape and the woman pruning beside him, he burns the contract — but tells Jonah nothing. Emotional beat: loyalty tested in secret.

chapters.title: Blossom and Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Late blossoms arrive against all odds, and the town rallies for a blossom festival on the orchard grounds. Dancing under string lights, Jonah and Elias finally kiss — then she finds the burned contract's ashes in his stove and feels betrayed all over again. Emotional beat: joy collapsing into doubt.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Cornered by Jonah's fury, Elias confesses everything: he left because her father's creditors threatened her, and he spent twelve years quietly paying down the Fairweather debt from afar. The deed was his way home, not his way out. Emotional beat: devastating honesty, too late to be easy.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A storm batters the coast the night before the foreclosure auction; the two race to save the heirloom trees, working side by side through wind and rain. Injured but alive, soaked and laughing, Jonah admits she stopped writing love stories the day he left. Emotional beat: fear stripped away into raw connection.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the auction, Marisol's developer bids aggressively. Jonah stands before the town and reads aloud from her unfinished novel — their story — declaring what the orchard means. Bidders waver; Elias pledges everything he owns. The hammer falls on a community trust bid organized by neighbors they'd both underestimated. Emotional beat: public vulnerability rewarded.

chapters.title: The Slow Garden
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue-adjacent. One year later: the orchard bears its first real harvest, Jonah finishes her novel with a living hero, and Elias plants a new tree carved with both their initials. She reflects that hearts aren't muscles to train but gardens to tend — slowly, together. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not found.
